
hoopvalue helps you measure NBA player value with advanced statistics. This
vignette walks through the included dataset and the main functions.

## The data

```{r}
library(hoopvalue)
dim(nba_players_2026)
head(nba_players_2026[, c("player", "team", "position", "games", "pts")])
```

## Efficiency and volume

`calc_true_shooting()` measures how efficiently a player scores, and
`calc_per_100()` puts totals on a per 100 possession scale.

```{r}
stars <- subset(nba_players_2026, player %in% c("Nikola Jokic", "Luka Doncic",
                                                "Shai Gilgeous-Alexander"))
data.frame(
  player = stars$player,
  ts_pct = round(calc_true_shooting(stars$pts, stars$fga, stars$fta), 3),
  pts_per_100 = round(calc_per_100(stars$pts, stars$possessions), 1)
)
```

## Overall value score

`player_value_score()` combines six advanced statistics into one score.

```{r}
scores <- player_value_score(nba_players_2026, min_minutes = 1000)
head(scores[, c("value_rank", "player", "team", "position", "value_score")], 10)
```

Weights let you decide what matters most. For example, a team looking for
rebounding and rim protection could weight those components more heavily:

```{r}
bigs <- player_value_score(nba_players_2026, min_minutes = 1000,
                           weights = c(reb_100 = 2, stocks_100 = 2))
head(bigs[, c("value_rank", "player", "team", "value_score")], 5)
```
